prompt: Starting a difficult new subject, which framing is most likely to keep a learner improving after early low scores?

options.text: 'I must top the class on the first test to prove I can do this'
'My goal this term is to master the core methods; early scores are information about what to practise next'
'I should avoid hard problems until I am sure I can score highly'
'Scores are the only honest measure, so I will judge every session by them'

explanation: A learning (mastery) goal treats early results as diagnostic information, which sustains practice after setbacks. A pure performance goal makes each low score feel like a verdict on ability.
